units.function: Embedded-Postgres end-to-end QA for local-encrypted routine Secret binding, execution-time resolution and precedence, cross-Company denial, value-free access events, deleted-Secret failure, revision restore reconciliation and legacy/null environment behavior.
units.dependencyDirection: Routine service writes versioned routine documents and Company Secret bindings; heartbeat adapter resolution merges Agent, project and routine env then asks Secret service to decrypt; access events record the routine consumer and executing Agent while the runtime config receives plaintext.
units.keyDataModels: Company/defaultResponsibleUserId; Agent adapter env; Company Secret/version/binding; local_encrypted provider; routine/revision/document/run; plain and latest secret_ref env bindings; resolved config, secretKeys and value-free manifest; Secret access event consumer/actor/configPath/outcome.
units.lifecycle: Create encrypted Secret; bind it to a routine snapshot; validate Company ownership; merge env layers at execution; decrypt into runtime memory and record access; fail safely after deletion; update and restore revisions with binding reconciliation; support legacy current-env and null-env paths.
units.testAssessment: The six source-level cases form a valuable vertical slice and explicitly inspect both manifest and database event serialization for plaintext absence. They also test tenant rejection and revision-binding restoration. The suite was skipped locally because embedded PostgreSQL is unavailable. The legacy test inserts a null-revision run but bypasses retrieval by passing current routine.env directly, so it only partially proves the claimed fallback. Disabled and user-specific cases named by comments/history are absent, as are authorization, rotation, concurrency, cleanup and remote custody tests.
units.designRationale: Attach Secret authority to repeatable routine configuration rather than requiring permanent Agent-wide grants, preserve precedence across configuration layers and maintain binding indexes in sync with versioned routine snapshots.
units.companyOsProblem: Reusable work templates need narrowly scoped credentials and data access that can be resolved for a specific execution without leaking through the cloud control plane, Connector payload, API, audit log or evidence bundle, while a real human remains accountable for the grant.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT the binding index, cross-Company validation, value-free manifest/access event, execution-time resolution, deleted-reference failure and revision reconciliation. Replace implicit routine authority with a versioned human-approved Secret/DataGrant containing purpose, Agent/work contract, audience, scope, fixed version or explicit rotation policy, expiry and revocation. Resolve only inside the authorized local/managed execution node; return short-lived secret-free attestation and scrub process state on every terminal path. Treat legacy current-env fallback as migration-only and record the effective snapshot.
units.responsibilityConflict: The routine can grant a Secret to an Agent that has no direct binding, yet creation/restoration passes no authenticated human context and the seeded responsible user is unused. Precedence silently changes effective authority, while latest/current-env fallback can make two nominally identical runs consume different credentials. Company OS requires an accountable human grant and an immutable effective authorization snapshot per execution.
evidence: git history: three commits from 705c1b8d8115654835e1d902f3d5d015302c13b5 through ad961227f57a217655c9e05e5987e6d0e5524409 recorded in the read ledger
2026-08-19 focused Vitest: 1 file and 6 tests skipped because embedded PostgreSQL support was unavailable; no pass claimed
units.securityFindings: CRITICAL authority gap: routine creation/restoration can confer Secret use without an asserted authenticated accountable-human grant, purpose, expiry or approval. HIGH reproducibility gap: latest references and legacy current-env fallback can change effective credentials across runs. HIGH custody gap: server and execution resolver share plaintext/master-key responsibility; cloud/local separation and Connector exclusion are untested. HIGH lifecycle gap: rotation, disable/re-enable, revocation race, concurrent revision atomicity and terminal cleanup are absent. MEDIUM evidence gap: issueId and heartbeatRunId are deliberately null, weakening binding of access events to exact work/run evidence. POSITIVE: cross-Company references are rejected; manifest and access-event serialization are checked against plaintext; deleted Secret errors do not echo value; restored revisions reconcile binding indexes.
